summary: Stephen J. Laumakis specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Notre Dame (1985–1991), studying under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, George J. Tanabe, and David West, and was appointed Associate Professor of Philosophy at the University of St. Thomas in 1990.

Stephen Jenkins is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Harvard University, where his doctoral supervisors were Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey. Attested between 2010 and 2013, he served as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt.

Stephen Meredyth Edwardes (1873–1927) was a historian and Indologist educated at Eton College (~1887–1891) and Christ Church (~1891–1894). His career included serving as secretary of the Indo-British Association and editor of the Indian Antiquary in 1923.

Stephen Montagu Burrows (1856–1935) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Eton College (~1868–1874) and earned his B.A. from Exeter College, Oxford, where he studied from around 1875 to 1879.

Stephen N. Hay (1925–2001) was an Indologist and historian educated at Swarthmore College and Harvard University (Ph.D. ~1957). He taught at the University of Chicago (1956–1964), Harvard (1964–1966), and the University of California, Santa Barbara (1966–1991).

Stephen Prothero (born 1960) is a religious studies scholar who earned his B.A. at Yale and his Ph.D. at Harvard (~1986–1990) under William R. Hutchison. He became the C. Allyn and Elizabeth V. Russell Professor Emeritus of Religion in America at Boston University (~1996).

Stephen R. Bokenkamp (born 1949) is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at UC Berkeley (~1974–1986). He served as Associate Professor of Classical Chinese at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2007) and Professor of Chinese at Arizona State University (~2007).
Stephen Suen is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009), where he studied under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti.

Stephen Wootton Bushell (1844–1908) was a Sinologist and historian who earned an MD from the University of London (~1866–1868). After early hospital appointments in London, he served as physician to the British Embassy in Beijing from 1868 to 1900.

Steve Odin (born 1953) is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who completed graduate studies under David A. Dilworth and Edward S. Casey at Stony Brook University (~1975–1980). In 1982, he joined the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa as Professor of Philosophy.

Steven Collins (1950–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich. His academic posts included positions at Bristol, Indiana University Bloomington, and the University of Chicago as Chester D. Tripp Professor in the Humanities (1991).

Steven Edward Lindquist works in Indology and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin in 2005 under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle, and he has held an academic post at Concordia University.

Steven Heine (born 1950) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at Temple University (1976–1980). He held faculty posts at Villanova, La Salle, and Pennsylvania State University before becoming a professor at Florida International University in 1997.

Steven Lukes (born 1941) is a philosopher and sociologist educated at Oxford under E. E. Evans-Pritchard. He held posts at Balliol College, Oxford (1966–1987), the European University Institute, the University of Siena, LSE, and New York University (~2000–2021).

Steven Neal Weinberger is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA from Amherst College and his MA and PhD (2003) from the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding an attested post there in 2006.

Steven Vose is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history. After completing his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (2006–2013), he held faculty positions at Florida International University (2013–2021), Colorado College (2021–2022), and the University of Colorado Denver (2022).

Stewart McFarlane is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. His academic career includes appointments in the Department of Religious Studies at Lancaster University, attested in 1991 and 2001.

Sthaneshwar Timalsina (born 1965) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religion who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held faculty posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, San Diego State University, and Stony Brook University.

Sthira Bhattacharya is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Bhattacharya pursued a Ph.D. at the University of Chicago from 2019 to 2026 and was appointed there as a Postdoctoral Teaching Fellow in 2026.

Stig Wikander (1908–1983) was a Swedish scholar of Indology, Iranian-Central Asian studies, and linguistics. Educated at Uppsala under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, he held posts at Lund University and served as Chair of Sanskrit and Comparative Indo-European Philology at Uppsala (1953–1974).
